affected_versions.reasoning: The OSV range introduced=0 is technically correct per the advisory, but the vulnerable component — the basic_auth.ini file and MLflow's authentication plugin — was introduced in mlflow 2.x, not 1.x. The conda-forge mlflow-pipelines versions (1.28.0, 1.29.0, 1.30.0) are all 1.x releases that almost certainly do not contain the auth plugin. If confirmed that the auth plugin is absent from 1.x, these versions should be removed from affected_versions. Human verification of the mlflow 1.x codebase is needed to confirm this.

mlflow-pipelines::GHSA-gq3w-7jj3-x7gr.notes: CVE-2026-2635 has a 2026 year prefix, suggesting this is a newly assigned future-dated CVE. The fix reference points to mlflow v3.8.0rc0, which is significantly newer than the mlflow-pipelines 1.30.0 package. The key question is whether mlflow 1.x (as shipped in mlflow-pipelines) ever contained the basic_auth.ini file. If not, all three conda-forge affected versions should be removed. Human review of the mlflow 1.30.0 source tree is recommended.
mlflow-pipelines::GHSA-gq3w-7jj3-x7gr.rationale: The OSV range covers all mlflow versions from 0 up to (not including) 3.8.0rc0, and the conda-forge mlflow-pipelines package ships version 1.30.0, which falls well within this range. The vulnerability involves hard-coded default credentials in the basic_auth.ini configuration file used by MLflow's authentication plugin, allowing authentication bypass. However, it is important to note that MLflow's basic authentication feature was introduced in much later versions (mlflow 2.x) and was not part of the mlflow 1.x codebase that mlflow-pipelines wraps. Version 1.30.0 predates the introduction of the basic_auth plugin, so this specific file and the associated authentication mechanism are likely not present in mlflow 1.x. The affected_versions listing of 1.28.0, 1.29.0, and 1.30.0 may be over-broad for this particular vulnerability since the vulnerable component (basic_auth.ini and related auth plugin) was introduced after the 1.x series.

runtime_applicability.reasoning: The vulnerability involves a hard-coded default password in the basic_auth.ini configuration file, which is part of MLflow's authentication plugin introduced in the 2.x series. Since mlflow-pipelines wraps mlflow 1.30.0, this authentication component may not exist in the shipped package. A human reviewer should verify whether mlflow 1.30.0 includes the basic_auth plugin at all.

severity_in_conda_context.reasoning: If the basic_auth plugin is absent from mlflow 1.30.0, the severity would effectively be zero for this package. If present, the CVSS 9.8 critical score would be appropriate since it allows complete authentication bypass over the network. The applicability needs to be confirmed first.

affected_versions.reasoning: The OSV range introduced=0, fixed=2.9.2 covers all versions before 2.9.2. All three conda-forge mlflow-pipelines versions (1.28.0, 1.29.0, 1.30.0) are in the 1.x series and are correctly identified as affected. No conda-forge mlflow-pipelines version at 2.9.2 or later exists, so there are no false inclusions to remove.

mlflow-pipelines::GHSA-hh8p-p8mp-gqhm.notes: Similar to GHSA-fmxj-6h9g-6vw3, the mlflow-pipelines conda-forge package is stuck at version 1.30.0 with no upgrade path within the same package. Users needing the fix must migrate to the main mlflow conda-forge package at version 2.9.2 or later.
mlflow-pipelines::GHSA-hh8p-p8mp-gqhm.openvex_action_statement: Users of mlflow-pipelines on conda-forge should be aware that no fixed version is available within the mlflow-pipelines package. Consider migrating to the standard mlflow package at version 2.9.2 or later, which contains the fix for this path traversal/RCE vulnerability. Avoid exposing the mlflow tracking server to untrusted or unauthenticated network access when using mlflow-pipelines 1.30.0 or earlier.
mlflow-pipelines::GHSA-hh8p-p8mp-gqhm.rationale: The OSV range covers all mlflow versions from 0 up to (not including) 2.9.2, and the conda-forge mlflow-pipelines package ships version 1.30.0, which falls within this vulnerable range. This is a path traversal vulnerability enabling remote code execution, affecting mlflow's core artifact and model serving functionality. All three listed conda-forge affected versions (1.28.0, 1.29.0, 1.30.0) are well below the fixed version 2.9.2 and are correctly identified as vulnerable. No fixed version of mlflow-pipelines is available on conda-forge, as the package only goes up to 1.30.0 which is part of the mlflow 1.x series. The vulnerability is in core mlflow server functionality that is accessible at runtime when the tracking server is used.

runtime_applicability.reasoning: This path traversal vulnerability enabling command execution is in the core mlflow server and model serving components, which are central to the mlflow-pipelines use case. When users operate the MLflow tracking server or serve models, the vulnerable code path is reachable from the network without authentication.

severity_in_conda_context.reasoning: The CVSS 9.8 critical score reflects unauthenticated network-accessible remote code execution via path traversal, which is appropriate for the conda context. MLflow tracking servers are commonly exposed within data science infrastructure, making this a realistic high-severity threat for mlflow-pipelines users.

statements.action_statement: Users of mlflow-pipelines on conda-forge should be aware that no fixed version is available within the mlflow-pipelines package. Consider migrating to the standard mlflow package at version 2.9.2 or later, which contains the fix for this path traversal/RCE vulnerability. Avoid exposing the mlflow tracking server to untrusted or unauthenticated network access when using mlflow-pipelines 1.30.0 or earlier.

Upgrade to langchain-community >= 0.0.27 on conda-forge. The latest conda-forge version 0.4.2 is not affected. Users on historical 0.0.x conda-forge builds at or below 0.0.26 should upgrade immediately due to the critical severity of unsafe pickle deserialization in TFIDFRetriever.load_local.

Upgrade to gevent >= 23.9.0 (conda-forge latest is 26.5.0, which is fixed). Historical conda-forge builds at or below 22.10.2 remain vulnerable and should not be used in any deployment that exposes gevent's WSGIServer to untrusted input.

statements.impact_statement: This advisory has been formally withdrawn. The original finding only affected gradio 4.36.1 and was retracted because exploitation requires running specifically crafted user-authored code, not an external attacker triggering the code path. The conda-forge package at 6.17.3 is well beyond the single affected version, and the withdrawn advisory carries no actionable security relevance.

statements.action_statement: No fixed version of imgaug exists upstream or on conda-forge. Users should avoid using the BackgroundAugmenter class in multicore.py in untrusted or network-facing environments, or ensure that the multiprocessing queue cannot be influenced by untrusted input. Monitor the upstream repository at https://github.com/aleju/imgaug for a patched release.

No fixed version is currently available upstream (OSV uses last_affected rather than fixed). Users should avoid exposing the Horovod KVStore HTTP server to untrusted networks, use network-level access controls, and monitor for an upstream patch. Upgrade as soon as a patched release is available on conda-forge.

No fixed upstream version is currently indicated in the OSV record. Users should restrict network access to the Horovod rendezvous server port and avoid running horovod elastic training in environments where the rendezvous endpoint is reachable by untrusted parties. Monitor upstream and conda-forge for a patched release and upgrade immediately when available.

No upstream fix has been released yet (last_affected is 3.46.0.7, affects_future is True). Users should monitor the h2oai/h2o-3 project for a patch release and upgrade as soon as one is available on conda-forge. Consider restricting network access to the H2O REST API as a temporary mitigation.

Upgrade to h2o-py version 3.46.0.6 on conda-forge, which contains the upstream fix (commit ac1d642b4d86f10a02d75974055baf2a4b2025ac). All conda-forge versions prior to 3.46.0.6 remain vulnerable. Users who cannot upgrade should restrict network access to the H2O REST API endpoints POST /99/ImportSQLTable and POST /3/SaveToHiveTable.

Upgrade jupyter_enterprise_gateway to version 3.3.0 on conda-forge, which contains the fix for the ContainerProcessProxy._enforce_prohibited_ids bypass. The latest conda-forge version (3.3.0) is patched; all prior versions from 2.0.0 to 3.2.3 remain vulnerable.

Upgrade kedro to version 0.19.9 or later (the current conda-forge latest is 1.3.1, which is not affected). Historical conda-forge builds at versions 0.15.9 through 0.19.8 listed in affected_versions are vulnerable to this deserialization RCE.

Upgrade kedro to version 1.3.0 or later. The current conda-forge latest (1.3.1) includes the fix that validates logging configuration before passing it to dictConfig(). All conda-forge builds at versions 0.15.9 through 1.2.0 as listed in affected_versions are vulnerable to this RCE via malicious logging configuration.
